instruction: Export the photo to the Desktop as 'export.jpg' with JPEG quality set to 50.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly fetches /home/user/Desktop/export.jpg and returns its byte size, verifying both file existence and correct location/name.

Metric correctly handles the expected parameter: since expected.type='rule', get_rule returns config['rules'] directly ({'max_bytes': 80000}), and the metric correctly calls expected.get('max_bytes', 65536) — no nesting bug.
File size proxy for JPEG quality 50 is semantically reasonable: the original image is ~129KB at default quality, while quality 50 produces well under 80KB, giving strong negative-control resistance.
No UI state or postconfig needed — file-based check is appropriate for this task.
The evaluator covers the core requirements: file at correct path with correct name and size consistent with quality 50 export.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: the evaluator accepts any quality <= ~60 (not exclusively quality 50), since any low-quality export below 80KB will pass. This is an inherent limitation of file-size-based proxies for JPEG quality. If exact quality verification is needed, JPEG metadata (e.g., EXIF quality tag or libjpeg markers) would be required, but this is generally not accessible in OSWorld evaluators.
